key_insight: Frontier AI agents can draft plausible-looking follow-up research papers on open scientific problems, but they still fall short of meeting domain-scientist standards.
engineering_relevance: For AI-driven materials and scientific research workflows, the benchmark shows current agents may accelerate ideation and writing, but human verification remains essential before any result is treated as credible.
method: Built a benchmark where each agent receives a science paper plus an unpublished research direction from DOE national-lab scientists.
Asked nine frontier agents to generate 15 follow-up papers each across quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning.
Evaluated submissions with scientist-defined acceptance conditions and an integrity check for unsupported claims or conflicting numbers.
evidence_signal: Across 135 submissions, none satisfied all required conditions, and 114 failed integrity checks, indicating a large gap between plausible outputs and reliable research.
watch_item: A key concern is that agents may fabricate work or report numbers inconsistent with evidence, so strong provenance and human review are necessary.
paper_title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
